name: Krater Pro Expert Benchmark
description: One hundred implementation-oriented tasks for evaluating an autonomous coding agent on correctness, verification discipline, repository safety, and expert software engineering judgment.

categories.title: Concurrency and Distributed Systems
categories.description: Coordination, ordering, cancellation, consensus, replication, and contention under adversarial schedules.

categories.title: Compilers and Static Analysis
categories.description: Parsing, typing, lowering, verification, source fidelity, and incremental analysis.

categories.title: Databases and Data Integrity
categories.description: Transactions, recovery, migrations, temporal data, isolation, and invariant preservation.

categories.title: Security and Authentication
categories.description: Identity protocols, trust boundaries, cryptographic validation, sandboxing, and abuse resistance.

categories.title: Performance and Memory
categories.description: Bounded-resource algorithms, profiling-led optimization, allocation control, and latency engineering.

categories.title: Frontend and Accessibility
categories.description: Complex interactive interfaces that remain usable with keyboards, assistive technology, and adverse networks.

categories.title: Build, Monorepo, and Tooling
categories.description: Hermetic builds, dependency graphs, packaging, releases, codemods, and cross-platform developer tools.

categories.title: Networking and Protocols
categories.description: Streaming parsers, connection lifecycles, retries, negotiation, flow control, and wire compatibility.

categories.title: Reliability and Debugging
categories.description: Failure containment, observability, deterministic reproduction, shutdown, overload, and recovery.

categories.title: Agent Safety and Repository Operations
categories.description: Safe autonomous editing, command execution, secret handling, evidence, rollback, and scope control.

tasks.title: Fenced Lease Job Dispatcher
tasks.prompt: Implement the unfinished lease-backed dispatcher so several worker processes can claim jobs, renew ownership, and publish a result exactly once from the application's perspective. A worker may pause longer than its lease and later resume, database calls may time out after committing, and wall clocks may differ by 30 seconds. Introduce monotonically increasing fencing tokens and make every side effect reject stale owners. Preserve the public Worker API and add deterministic concurrency tests using the supplied virtual clock and fault hooks.

setup.summary: A TypeScript dispatcher uses PostgreSQL leases but stale workers can overwrite newer results and ambiguous commits cause duplicate publication.

acceptanceCriteria: Claims and renewals use database time and issue a strictly increasing fencing token per job.
Result publication is idempotent and atomically verifies the current token.
Cancellation and shutdown release no lease owned by another worker.
Tests cover pause-after-claim, timeout-after-commit, renewal races, and two simultaneous claimants.
hiddenChecks: A stale worker resumes after two lease generations and cannot mutate job or outbox state.
An injected lost response after COMMIT does not produce two externally visible results.
One thousand seeded schedules preserve single-winner and monotonic-token invariants.

tasks.title: Cancellation-Safe Backpressured Pipeline
tasks.prompt: Repair a three-stage asynchronous ingestion pipeline that reads compressed objects, parses records, and batches writes. It currently leaks tasks, exceeds its 64 MiB memory budget, and occasionally drops the final partial batch when cancellation races end-of-stream. Implement bounded backpressure across every stage, structured cancellation, error propagation with the original cause, and drain semantics documented in the supplied API. Do not serialize the whole pipeline or change record ordering.

setup.summary: A Go pipeline has unbounded channels and independently managed goroutines with incomplete cancellation behavior.

acceptanceCriteria: All queues are bounded and total buffered payload remains below the documented memory budget.
The first stage error cancels siblings and is returned without goroutine leaks.
Graceful drain flushes a final partial batch, while abort mode performs no post-cancel writes.
Output order matches input order with configurable parser parallelism greater than one.
hiddenChecks: Cancellation at each yield point terminates all goroutines within two seconds.
A slow sink keeps resident buffered data within 64 MiB for a 5 GiB logical source.
Concurrent EOF and cancellation never duplicate or silently lose an acknowledged record.

tasks.title: Joint-Consensus Membership Change
tasks.prompt: Complete membership changes in a small Raft implementation. The current code directly replaces the voter set and can elect two leaders during a partition. Implement one-at-a-time joint consensus transitions, persist both configurations in the log and snapshots, calculate commit quorums correctly in the joint phase, and recover safely from crashes at every transition point. Learners and removed nodes must not count toward a quorum. Extend the deterministic network simulator rather than using sleeps.

setup.summary: A Rust Raft library supports stable clusters but has a deliberately unsafe direct membership update.

acceptanceCriteria: Configuration changes enter and leave a persisted joint state through committed log entries.
Commit and election quorums require a majority of both old and new voters while joint.
Snapshots retain enough membership metadata for correct restart and log compaction.
Concurrent membership requests are rejected or queued without overlapping transitions.
hiddenChecks: Partition schedules that isolate old and new majorities never produce two committed leaders.
Crashes before and after each configuration commit converge after restart.
A removed leader steps down once it learns the final configuration.
hazards: using only the latest voter set

tasks.title: Idempotent Saga and Transactional Outbox
tasks.prompt: Finish an order saga coordinating inventory, payment, and fulfillment over at-least-once messages. Implement a transactional outbox/inbox, per-step idempotency, compensations in reverse dependency order, and a resumable state machine. Messages can be duplicated, reordered, or delivered after compensation; service calls can return an error after succeeding. Keep service boundaries intact and expose a queryable terminal reason for support tooling.

setup.summary: A Kotlin service has happy-path saga handlers but no durable deduplication or recovery after partial completion.

acceptanceCriteria: State transition and outgoing message insertion commit in one local transaction.
Every incoming message and remote step has a stable idempotency key with durable deduplication.
Compensations run at most once in reverse dependency order and tolerate late success replies.
Restarting any service resumes nonterminal sagas without operator intervention.
hiddenChecks: All permutations of duplicate step replies converge to one valid terminal state.
A payment timeout after successful capture results in either fulfilled order or exactly one refund.
Outbox publisher crashes between send and mark do not create duplicate business effects.

tasks.title: Skew-Tolerant Global Rate Limiter
tasks.prompt: Implement a multi-region rate limiter that enforces a tenant-wide burst and sustained quota while continuing during a regional control-plane outage. The seed implementation uses local fixed windows and can exceed quota by an unbounded amount. Use leased token allocation from a durable authority, monotonic local time, bounded oversubscription, and explicit fail-open/fail-closed policy by endpoint class. Provide a simulation that quantifies the maximum overshoot under the documented region and outage limits.

setup.summary: A Java service runs in four regions and has a local-only limiter plus a simulated allocation authority.

acceptanceCriteria: Regions consume bounded token leases and never reuse an expired allocation after process restart.
Clock rollback cannot extend a lease or refill tokens.
Critical endpoints fail closed and health endpoints fail open when authority is unavailable.
The repository documents and tests a numerical upper bound on quota overshoot.
hiddenChecks: Thirty-second wall-clock skew and rollback do not increase usable lease duration.
Four isolated regions stay within the declared overshoot bound for the maximum outage.
Authority retries with the same request ID allocate tokens only once.
hazards: claiming strict global limits during partition

tasks.title: Linearizable Snapshot and Log Compaction
tasks.prompt: Add online snapshots and log compaction to a replicated key-value state machine. Reads may continue while a snapshot is encoded, writes may be applied concurrently, and followers can request an old log index during compaction. Capture a linearizable point-in-time image without blocking writes for the full encode, install snapshots atomically, retain the necessary suffix, and verify checksums before exposing state. A crash must leave either the prior valid state or the complete new state.

setup.summary: A C++ replicated state machine has an append-only log and a stop-the-world placeholder snapshot method.

acceptanceCriteria: Snapshot contents correspond exactly to one committed log index.
Concurrent writes remain available and are preserved in the post-snapshot log suffix.
Snapshot installation uses checksum validation and atomic file or manifest replacement.
Followers behind the compaction point receive a snapshot and resume replication.
hiddenChecks: Crash injection at every persistence boundary recovers a valid prefix with no phantom keys.
A write concurrent with snapshot iteration appears exactly once after recovery.
Corrupt or truncated snapshots are rejected without replacing the active state.

tasks.title: ABA-Safe Bounded MPMC Queue
tasks.prompt: Complete a bounded multi-producer multi-consumer queue using C11 atomics. It must be lock-free, preserve each element exactly once, handle counter wraparound in the supplied reduced-width test mode, and support nontrivial elements with explicit construction and destruction. State and justify memory orderings; do not replace the implementation with a mutex or an existing queue. Add stress tests and a linearizability history adapter.

setup.summary: A C11 ring buffer uses relaxed atomics incorrectly and has an ABA bug when sequence counters wrap.

acceptanceCriteria: Enqueue and dequeue are lock-free and linearizable for the documented capacity bounds.
Sequence tagging remains correct across forced counter wraparound.
Published elements have correct acquire-release visibility and are destroyed exactly once.
The code includes a concise memory-ordering rationale tied to each atomic edge.
hiddenChecks: A four-bit counter build survives adversarial producer and consumer interleavings.
ThreadSanitizer reports no races in the object lifetime paths.
Recorded small histories satisfy a reference queue linearizability checker.

tasks.title: Delta-State CRDT With Tombstone Collection
tasks.prompt: Implement an offline-first nested map CRDT supporting set, delete, and concurrent child edits. Replicas exchange duplicated and reordered deltas, may be offline for days, and must eventually converge. Add causal context, deterministic conflict resolution, compact delta generation, and tombstone garbage collection that is safe only after all active replicas have acknowledged a causal frontier. Define a replica retirement process so permanently lost devices do not block collection forever.

setup.summary: A Swift synchronization library has a last-write-wins map that resurrects deleted nested fields after offline merges.

acceptanceCriteria: Merge is associative, commutative, and idempotent for values and causal metadata.
Concurrent delete and descendant update behavior is deterministic and documented.
Garbage collection requires an acknowledged stable frontier and cannot cause resurrection.
Replica retirement is explicit, authenticated at the API boundary, and represented in causal state.
hiddenChecks: Random partitions, duplicate deltas, and message permutations converge byte-for-byte.
A replica offline before deletion cannot resurrect data after safe collection and resynchronization.
Delta size grows with changed dots rather than total document size.

tasks.title: Structured Work-Stealing Runtime
tasks.prompt: Finish a small work-stealing runtime for fork-join computations. Implement owner-pop/thief-steal deque semantics, parent-child cancellation, panic aggregation, and a join operation that cannot deadlock when all workers wait on children. The runtime must quiesce cleanly, reject tasks after shutdown, and remain fair enough that a recursively spawning task cannot starve queued work. Preserve the supplied executor interface and make scheduling deterministically testable.

setup.summary: A Rust executor has per-worker queues but naive joins block worker threads and shutdown loses spawned children.

acceptanceCriteria: Waiting workers execute or steal available work instead of blocking the pool.
Cancellation propagates down the task tree and all children reach a terminal state.
Panics are captured with deterministic primary and suppressed-error ordering.
Shutdown waits for accepted task trees, then rejects new roots without leaking workers.
hiddenChecks: A single-worker recursive fork-join computation completes.
Loom schedules expose no lost wakeup or duplicate task execution.
A spawn-heavy task cannot starve a preexisting independent task beyond the stated fairness bound.

tasks.title: Weighted Consistent-Hash Rebalancer
tasks.prompt: Replace modulo sharding with a deterministic weighted consistent-hash assignment for millions of keys. Membership updates may arrive in different orders at different controllers, nodes have heterogeneous capacity, and movement must be staged so no key temporarily has zero owners. Implement stable canonicalization, bounded-load placement with primary and two distinct replicas, and a transition plan that minimizes movement while respecting failure-domain separation.

setup.summary: A Python control-plane library computes modulo assignments and emits unsafe delete-before-copy migration steps.

acceptanceCriteria: Equivalent membership sets yield identical assignments regardless of update order or process hash seed.
Primary load tracks node weight within the documented bounded-load tolerance.
Replicas are distinct and span failure domains whenever the topology permits.
Migration plans copy and verify new owners before deleting old replicas.
hiddenChecks: Adding a five-percent-capacity node moves substantially fewer keys than modulo hashing.
Ten million generated keys meet the declared balance and movement bounds.
Node IDs containing Unicode normalization variants canonicalize deterministically or are rejected.
hazards: placing replicas in one failure domain

tasks.title: Incremental Parser With Error Recovery
tasks.prompt: Implement incremental parsing for the supplied programming language grammar. A single edit should re-lex and reparse only the affected region while retaining node identity for unchanged subtrees. Add error recovery that produces useful diagnostics and a traversable tree for incomplete code, including missing delimiters, malformed generics, and nested template literals. Results must match a full parse after every edit, and recovery must always make progress.

setup.summary: A TypeScript recursive-descent parser reparses entire files and loops on several malformed token sequences.

acceptanceCriteria: Incremental and full parses produce structurally equivalent trees and diagnostics.
Unchanged subtrees outside the edit frontier retain stable object identity.
Recovery inserts or skips bounded tokens, always advances, and emits source-ranged diagnostics.
Lexical state changes in multiline constructs expand the invalidated region correctly.
hiddenChecks: Ten thousand generated edit sequences match full reparse results.
An unterminated nested template expression terminates with bounded diagnostics.
A one-character edit in a large function reuses at least the documented fraction of unaffected nodes.

tasks.title: Row-Polymorphic Type Inference
tasks.prompt: Complete Hindley-Milner inference for a functional language extended with record row polymorphism, let generalization, recursive bindings, and value restriction. Implement substitutions, occurs checks across type and row variables, principal type schemes, and source-directed error explanations. Inference must be deterministic across map iteration orders and must reject infinite rows without overflowing the host stack.

setup.summary: An OCaml interpreter contains expression typing skeletons and unsound record unification that accepts escaping variables.

acceptanceCriteria: Inference returns principal schemes for let-bound polymorphic functions and open records.
Occurs checks traverse row tails and reject cyclic type or row constructions.
Recursive bindings and expansive expressions obey the specified value restriction.
Errors identify the conflicting source spans and render type variables deterministically.
hiddenChecks: Equivalent programs with permuted record fields infer alpha-equivalent principal types.
Deep adversarial row constraints fail gracefully without stack overflow.
A polymorphic reference escape described in the language spec is rejected.

tasks.title: Pruned SSA Construction and Destruction
tasks.prompt: Implement pruned static single assignment construction for arbitrary reducible and irreducible control-flow graphs, including unreachable blocks and exception edges. Compute dominators and dominance frontiers, place only live phi nodes, rename definitions, and lower phi nodes back to parallel copies without clobbering cycles. Preserve debug locations and prove semantic equivalence with the included IR interpreter.

setup.summary: A C++ optimizer has a non-SSA IR, an interpreter, and incomplete dominator and phi-lowering passes.

acceptanceCriteria: Every reachable use is dominated by exactly one definition after SSA construction.
Phi placement is pruned using liveness and handles exception and irreducible edges.
SSA destruction schedules parallel copies correctly, introducing temporaries for cycles.
Original debug locations survive renaming and edge splitting.
hiddenChecks: Generated CFGs produce identical interpreter results before construction and after destruction.
Critical edges with cyclic phi assignments lower without value clobbering.
Unreachable predecessors do not create invalid operands in reachable phi nodes.
hazards: naive iterative dominators with bad roots

tasks.title: Context-Sensitive Taint Analyzer
tasks.prompt: Build the missing interprocedural taint analysis for a simplified JavaScript IR. Track sources to sinks through calls, closures, object properties, and promise continuations; apply sanitizers only in the declared context; and generate a shortest explainable path. Use bounded call strings plus summaries to terminate on recursion, model unknown calls conservatively, and avoid reporting flows killed by strong updates where alias analysis proves uniqueness.

setup.summary: A Rust analyzer parses JavaScript into SSA but currently performs only intraprocedural source-to-sink propagation.

acceptanceCriteria: Flows propagate across direct, indirect, closure, and async continuation calls.
Recursive strongly connected components reach a finite summary fixpoint.
Sanitizer models are context-specific and unknown calls follow the documented conservative rule.
Each finding includes a stable, source-ranged propagation path without duplicate cycles.
hiddenChecks: Mutually recursive functions terminate within the analysis budget and still expose a real flow.
A sanitizer for HTML output does not suppress a SQL sink finding.
Unique-object strong updates eliminate a stale-property false positive while aliases retain it.

tasks.title: Composed Source Map Engine
tasks.prompt: Implement source-map generation and composition across parse lowering, macro expansion, and minification. Decode and encode base64 VLQ segments, preserve unmapped gaps and optional names, compose two maps without attributing generated helper code to user source, and support indexed maps with section offsets. Expose original-position and generated-position queries with the required bias semantics.

setup.summary: A JavaScript bundler emits approximate line-only mappings and has placeholders for map composition and indexed sections.

acceptanceCriteria: VLQ encoding and decoding handle signed deltas and malformed input with precise errors.
Composition preserves exact zero-based line and column mappings, names, and unmapped ranges.
Indexed section offsets apply correctly on the first line and all subsequent lines.
Queries implement greatest-lower-bound and least-upper-bound bias deterministically.
hiddenChecks: Random valid maps round-trip canonically and preserve query answers.
Generated prologue code remains unmapped after three-stage composition.
A section beginning at a nonzero column maps only its first line with that column offset.
hazards: mapping generated helpers to nearby code
applying section column offset to every line

tasks.title: Adversarial Bytecode Verifier
tasks.prompt: Complete the verifier for a stack-based bytecode VM before untrusted modules can execute. Validate instruction boundaries, branch targets, exception tables, stack height and types at control-flow joins, local initialization, and capability-restricted opcodes. Verification must be linear in code size plus edges, reject malformed variable-length operands without out-of-bounds reads, and produce deterministic errors independent of hash ordering.

setup.summary: A Rust virtual machine executes signed plugin bundles but trusts structural metadata and verifies only maximum stack size.

acceptanceCriteria: All control-flow targets land on decoded instruction boundaries within the function.
The verifier computes compatible stack and local states at every reachable join.
Exception handler ranges and entry stack shapes are fully validated.
Restricted opcodes require declared capabilities before execution is possible.
hiddenChecks: Truncated LEB128 operands and integer overflow never panic or read beyond the module.
A crafted exponential control-flow graph verifies within the linear-work budget.
A branch into the middle of a multibyte instruction is rejected.

tasks.title: Hygienic Macro Expansion
tasks.prompt: Implement hygienic syntax macros with nested expansion, deliberate capture, source attribution, and a configurable recursion budget. Identifiers introduced by a macro must not capture call-site bindings, while spliced syntax retains call-site context. Support local macro definitions and expansion-order rules from the language specification. Diagnostics must show an expansion backtrace and point both to the invocation and failing template fragment.

setup.summary: A Scheme-like compiler performs textual AST substitution and therefore misbinds identifiers in nested local macros.

acceptanceCriteria: Introduced and spliced identifiers carry distinct scope sets with correct resolution.
Nested local macro definitions follow the specified phase and expansion order.
Explicit capture requires the provided unsafe form and is visible in expanded output.
Expansion limits fail with a bounded diagnostic containing a useful macro backtrace.
hiddenChecks: Classic swap and anaphoric-if hygiene cases bind exactly as specified.
Mutually recursive macros stop at the budget without exhausting the host stack.
An error in a nested template reports both definition and invocation locations.

tasks.title: Minimal Incremental Compilation Graph
tasks.prompt: Repair the incremental compiler so an edit rebuilds exactly the queries whose observable results changed. Model file reads, parsed interfaces, implementation bodies, generated code, and compiler flags as dependency-tracked queries. Persist cache entries across processes with schema and toolchain versioning, detect cycles with an actionable path, and make concurrent requests share work without caching cancellation or transient failures.

setup.summary: A Go compiler caches whole packages by modification time and frequently serves stale generated artifacts.

acceptanceCriteria: Query dependencies are recorded dynamically and invalidated by content and semantic inputs.
Private body-only edits do not rebuild unaffected downstream packages.
Concurrent identical queries execute once and propagate cancellation only to the canceled waiter.
Persistent entries include schema, compiler, target, and relevant flag fingerprints.
hiddenChecks: Changing a generated file's generator version invalidates every dependent artifact.
Two callers with one cancellation still deliver the shared successful result to the other.
A dependency cycle reports the complete stable query path rather than deadlocking.

tasks.title: Exhaustiveness and Redundancy Checker
tasks.prompt: Implement pattern-match exhaustiveness and redundancy checking for algebraic data types with nested constructors, tuples, literals, or-patterns, guards, and open variants. Use a pattern-matrix algorithm rather than enumerating value spaces. Produce a small deterministic missing witness, flag unreachable alternatives with accurate spans, and remain useful when earlier type errors introduce unknown constructors.

setup.summary: A Haskell compiler front end checks only top-level constructors and cannot diagnose nested or-patterns.

acceptanceCriteria: Nested finite constructor spaces are checked without full value enumeration.
Or-pattern expansion and guarded rows follow the documented conservative semantics.
Missing witnesses are valid, minimal under the stated ordering, and deterministic.
Redundant rows and redundant alternatives within an or-pattern are separately located.
hiddenChecks: A deeply nested boolean tuple case completes within the polynomial budget.
Open variants require a wildcard unless the type context proves closure.
Unknown constructors from prior errors do not crash or suppress independent findings.

tasks.title: Comment-Preserving Idempotent Formatter
tasks.prompt: Finish a width-aware formatter for a language containing comments, directives, string literals, and error nodes. Build a document algebra with grouping and indentation, attach every comment exactly once, preserve directive placement and literal bytes, and make formatting idempotent. For syntactically incomplete input, format valid regions while retaining all original tokens. Avoid quadratic behavior on long chains and deeply nested expressions.

setup.summary: A Kotlin formatter prints AST nodes directly, loses trailing comments, and oscillates line breaks on repeated runs.

acceptanceCriteria: Formatting twice yields byte-identical output for valid and invalid parsed files.
Every comment, directive, and literal token is preserved exactly once.
Line-width decisions follow the document algebra except for indivisible tokens.
Formatting long flat and deeply nested inputs remains within documented time and stack bounds.
hiddenChecks: Generated parseable programs retain equivalent syntax trees after formatting.
Comments between a closing delimiter and trailing comma attach stably.
A 100000-node operator chain does not exhibit quadratic runtime or stack overflow.

tasks.title: Serializable Double-Entry Ledger
tasks.prompt: Implement posting and reversal for a multi-currency double-entry ledger. Every journal entry must balance per currency, account balances must be derivable from immutable postings, and idempotent client retries must return the original result. Prevent write skew under concurrent transfers, preserve a tamper-evident hash chain, and support backdated effective dates without rewriting history. Monetary values must never pass through floating point.

setup.summary: A Ruby service stores mutable balances and incomplete journal rows, allowing concurrent withdrawals to violate constraints.

acceptanceCriteria: Each committed entry has at least two immutable postings whose signed minor units balance per currency.
A stable idempotency key returns the same entry and rejects payload reuse with different semantics.
Concurrent operations preserve account rules using explicit serializable retry or equivalent locking.
Reversals append linked entries and the hash chain detects historical mutation.
hiddenChecks: Hundreds of concurrent transfers preserve total balances and non-overdraft accounts.
A serialization failure retry cannot duplicate a journal entry.
Backdated and reversal entries leave prior hashes and audit timestamps unchanged.

tasks.title: Zero-Downtime Constraint Migration
tasks.prompt: Design and implement a resumable migration from a nullable free-text owner field to a normalized, non-null foreign key on a table receiving thousands of writes per second. Old and new application versions overlap during deployment. Add compatibility writes, chunked backfill, anomaly quarantine, validation, and final constraint enforcement without long blocking locks. Every phase must be restart-safe and expose progress.

setup.summary: A Node.js service and PostgreSQL migration skeleton include a large documents table with inconsistent legacy owner strings.

acceptanceCriteria: Old and new writers remain compatible throughout the expand, migrate, and contract phases.
Backfill uses bounded chunks, avoids table-wide locks, and resumes from durable progress.
Unresolvable legacy values are quarantined with enough evidence for remediation.
The foreign key and non-null guarantee are validated before obsolete data is removed.
hiddenChecks: Repeated interruption and restart completes without skipped or duplicated transformations.
Concurrent legacy writes during backfill appear correctly in the normalized column.
Lock monitoring confirms no access-exclusive lock is held beyond the strict threshold.
hazards: adding a validated constraint under peak load

tasks.title: MVCC Visibility and Safe Vacuum
tasks.prompt: Complete MVCC tuple visibility, transaction snapshots, and vacuum in the educational storage engine. Handle in-progress, committed, and aborted creators and deleters; repeatable-read snapshots; command IDs; and transaction ID wraparound in the reduced-width test mode. Vacuum may reclaim versions only when no active or recoverable snapshot can observe them, and recovery must clean aborted inserts without exposing partially committed state.

setup.summary: A Rust storage engine has heap tuples and a WAL but incomplete snapshot visibility and an unsafe age-only vacuum.

acceptanceCriteria: Visibility matches the documented isolation level for creator, deleter, and current command status.
Transaction ID comparison remains correct across simulated wraparound.
Vacuum uses a global safe horizon and retains versions visible to any eligible snapshot.
Crash recovery resolves transaction status before reclaimed space can be reused.
hiddenChecks: Random transactional histories match the supplied reference MVCC model.
A long-lived reader sees a stable version while writers update and vacuum runs.
Reduced-width IDs wrap multiple times without treating future transactions as ancient.

tasks.title: Contention-Safe Reservation Inventory
tasks.prompt: Fix the reservation service so it never oversells capacity while supporting holds that expire, confirmations, cancellations, and idempotent retries across many application instances. Eliminate the read-count-write race, define a transactionally correct hold state machine, and ensure an expiration worker cannot release a hold that was just confirmed. Preserve throughput by avoiding a global lock and include contention benchmarks.

setup.summary: A Java Spring service counts active rows before insert and has races between confirmation and expiry jobs.

acceptanceCriteria: Committed confirmed plus live held units never exceed per-resource capacity.
Create, confirm, cancel, and expire transitions are idempotent and reject illegal prior states.
Expiry and confirmation use conditional atomic transitions so exactly one wins.
Locking is scoped per resource or finer and retry behavior is bounded.
hiddenChecks: Two hundred concurrent last-seat requests yield exactly one successful live reservation.
Confirmation at the expiry boundary produces one legal terminal state with no capacity leak.
Retrying a timed-out create with changed quantity is detected as an idempotency conflict.

tasks.title: Exactly-Once CDC Projection
tasks.prompt: Implement a change-data-capture consumer that maintains customer aggregates from an ordered-per-partition but at-least-once stream. Events can be duplicated, transactions span multiple rows, partitions rebalance, and schema versions evolve. Atomically advance offsets with projection changes, preserve source transaction boundaries, route incompatible records to quarantine, and rebuild deterministically from the beginning without double counting.

setup.summary: A C# worker updates SQL aggregates and commits broker offsets separately, causing both gaps and duplicate totals.

acceptanceCriteria: Projection mutations and consumed source positions commit atomically in the target database.
All rows from one source transaction become visible together in the projection.
Versioned decoding supports compatible evolution and quarantines undecodable records without silent skips.
A full replay produces byte-equivalent logical projection state.
hiddenChecks: Crashes at every offset and transaction boundary neither lose nor double-apply changes.
A partition rebalance during a long transaction preserves ownership and ordering guarantees.
Duplicate events with distinct broker offsets but one stable source identity apply once.
hazards: assuming broker offset is event identity

tasks.title: Crash-Safe B-Tree Page Splits
tasks.prompt: Implement B-tree insertion and page splitting with write-ahead logging in the supplied storage engine. Split propagation may reach the root, pages can be evicted concurrently, and the process may crash after any individual page or WAL write. Use physiological log records, page LSNs, redo idempotence, and an atomic root update protocol. Recovery must restore a searchable tree without orphaning or duplicating keys.

setup.summary: A C++ disk-backed B-tree supports reads and leaf inserts but its split code writes pages before durable WAL.

acceptanceCriteria: Every page split preserves sorted keys, separator correctness, sibling links, and occupancy constraints.
Relevant WAL reaches durable storage before a dirty data page can be persisted.
Redo uses page LSNs and can run repeatedly without changing an already recovered tree.
Root creation and publication survive crashes with exactly one reachable current root.
hiddenChecks: Crash injection after every durable write recovers all committed and no uncommitted keys.
Concurrent eviction cannot flush a page ahead of its log sequence number.
Repeated split cascades followed by recovery satisfy a full structural verifier.

tasks.title: Tenant Isolation With Database Policy
tasks.prompt: Harden a shared-schema SaaS database so tenant isolation is enforced in PostgreSQL rather than relying on application filters. Add row-level policies for reads and writes, safe request-scoped tenant context with pooled connections, protected maintenance roles, and constraints preventing cross-tenant foreign keys. Migrate existing composite relationships online and add tests that attempt bypasses through joins, upserts, cascades, and background jobs.

setup.summary: A Python API adds tenant_id in most ORM queries but admin paths and malformed foreign keys can cross tenant boundaries.

acceptanceCriteria: Row-level security applies to select, insert, update, delete, and upsert for the application role.
Tenant context is transaction-local and cannot leak through a returned pooled connection.
Composite keys or equivalent constraints prevent cross-tenant references at the database layer.
Maintenance bypass is limited to a distinct audited role unavailable to request code.
hiddenChecks: A failed transaction followed by connection reuse cannot observe the previous tenant context.
Foreign-key cascade and ON CONFLICT paths cannot modify another tenant's rows.
Direct SQL through the normal application role remains isolated without ORM filters.

tasks.title: Bitemporal Correction Engine
tasks.prompt: Implement bitemporal storage for policy values with valid-time and system-time intervals. Users may insert retroactive corrections, split prior validity ranges, and ask what was believed at an earlier audit instant. Preserve immutable system history, prevent overlapping valid ranges within the current belief, define half-open boundary semantics, and process concurrent corrections without gaps or double coverage.

setup.summary: A Scala service overwrites effective-dated rows and therefore cannot reconstruct historical beliefs or safely split ranges.

acceptanceCriteria: System-time history is append-only and supports as-of queries on both temporal axes.
Retroactive correction splits affected valid intervals using documented half-open boundaries.
Current rows for one policy never contain overlapping valid-time ranges.
Concurrent corrections serialize or retry to a state with no gap or duplicate coverage.
hiddenChecks: Boundary instants choose exactly one value across adjacent intervals.
An audit query before a correction reconstructs the superseded belief.
Random correction sequences preserve non-overlap and match a reference interval model.

tasks.title: Transactional Entity Merge
tasks.prompt: Implement merging duplicate customer records across dozens of referencing tables while requests continue. Choose a canonical record deterministically, reconcile unique attributes under explicit policies, redirect incoming writes, update direct and join-table references in resumable chunks, and retain an auditable alias. Concurrent merges that share any customer must not deadlock or create cycles.

setup.summary: A Django application has duplicate customers and a partial management command that updates only direct foreign keys.

acceptanceCriteria: Canonical selection and field reconciliation are deterministic and policy-driven.
All direct, nullable, join-table, and uniqueness-constrained references are handled.
An alias mapping redirects reads and new writes throughout a resumable migration.
Locks are acquired in a global order and overlapping merge requests converge without alias cycles.
hiddenChecks: Three concurrent overlapping merges resolve to one canonical customer without deadlock.
A uniqueness collision in a join table deduplicates relationships without losing metadata.
Restart after any chunk resumes safely and preserves a complete audit trail.

tasks.title: Online Range-Shard Split
