tasks.title: Resilient Streaming Agent Console
tasks.prompt: Build the Krater Pro web console for a streaming coding-agent session. Render interleaved assistant text, tool calls, diffs, approvals, and terminal output from an ordered event stream; reconnect from the last event without duplication; and virtualize long sessions. Users must pause auto-follow, navigate events by keyboard, inspect diffs accessibly, cancel generation, and distinguish pending, failed, retried, and completed operations without exposing the API key to the browser.

setup.summary: A Vite React shell displays plain text chunks but duplicates content after reconnect and embeds provider credentials client-side.

acceptanceCriteria: Events reconcile by stable sequence and operation identity across disconnect, retry, and resume.
Auto-follow pauses on user navigation and resumes only through an explicit, accessible control.
Tool, approval, terminal, and diff states have semantic labels, keyboard navigation, and restrained announcements.
Provider credentials remain server-side and cancellation reaches the active upstream request.
hiddenChecks: Reconnect replay plus a live duplicate renders every event exactly once in order.
A 100000-event session stays responsive and retains logical keyboard position through virtualization.
Browser bundles, storage, network requests, and rendered errors contain no API-key canary.
hazards: shipping API credentials to the client

tasks.title: Hermetic Remote-Cached Task Graph
tasks.prompt: Implement a monorepo task runner that constructs a dependency DAG, executes independent work in parallel, and safely reuses a content-addressed local or remote cache. Cache identity must include declared files, dependency outputs, command, toolchain, selected environment, platform, and executable metadata. Run tasks in a sandbox that detects undeclared reads and writes, restore outputs atomically, and never publish cache entries from failed or canceled tasks.

setup.summary: A Rust task runner hashes source mtimes and command names, producing stale cross-platform cache hits and output races.

acceptanceCriteria: The graph detects cycles with a stable explanatory path and schedules only dependency-ready tasks.
Cache keys cover all declared semantic inputs and dependency artifact digests.
Sandbox observation reports undeclared access and keeps task writes outside the workspace until success.
Cache download, validation, restoration, and upload are atomic and cancellation-safe.
hiddenChecks: Changing executable mode, toolchain version, or a permitted environment variable invalidates the entry.
A malicious truncated remote artifact cannot partially overwrite workspace outputs.
Two identical concurrent tasks share or race safely without publishing an incomplete cache object.

tasks.title: Correct Dual ESM and CJS Packaging
tasks.prompt: Repair a TypeScript library's packaging so Node ESM, Node CommonJS, bundlers, and TypeScript resolve one coherent public API. Define conditional exports without the dual-package state hazard, generate declarations with matching subpaths, hide internals, preserve tree shaking, and include source maps that point to published sources. Add consumer fixtures that install the packed tarball rather than importing the workspace.

setup.summary: A pnpm package publishes mixed module syntax, duplicated singleton state, missing subpath types, and untested source paths.

acceptanceCriteria: Import, require, and documented subpaths resolve with matching runtime and declaration shapes.
ESM and CommonJS consumers observe one singleton behavior where the API promises shared identity.
Undocumented internals are blocked by exports and ESM output remains statically tree-shakeable.
Packed-tarball fixtures cover supported Node and TypeScript resolution modes.
hiddenChecks: A consumer using NodeNext resolves every public subpath without declaration fallback.
Importing and requiring through a bridge does not initialize the library twice.
Published source maps contain no absolute build-machine paths.
hazards: testing workspace source instead of tarball
separate mutable ESM and CJS instances

tasks.title: Semantic Monorepo Boundary Enforcer
tasks.prompt: Implement a repository rule engine that enforces package layering, ownership, public entry points, and forbidden dependency classes across TypeScript, generated code, dynamic imports, and test-only edges. Resolve imports with the same aliases and exports conditions as the compiler, report the shortest violating path, support narrow reviewed exceptions with expiry, and cache analysis incrementally without missing changes to configuration or package metadata.

setup.summary: A Node.js lint script matches import text with regular expressions and misses aliases, re-exports, and dynamic edges.

acceptanceCriteria: Resolution matches repository compiler settings, package exports, and supported import forms.
Policies cover layer direction, public API, owner, runtime-to-dev, and generated-edge rules.
Violations include source span, resolved target, policy, and shortest explanatory dependency path.
Exceptions require owner, rationale, narrow scope, and parseable expiration.
hiddenChecks: A forbidden dependency hidden behind two legal re-export packages is reported with its path.
Changing tsconfig paths or package exports invalidates affected cached resolutions.
An expired wildcard exception cannot silently suppress a new violation.

tasks.title: Sound Affected-Test Selection
tasks.prompt: Build an affected-test selector for a polyglot monorepo using the merge-base diff, static and observed dependencies, generated artifacts, runtime configuration, and ownership boundaries. It may over-select but must not omit a test whose behavior can change. Explain every selected test, fall back safely for unknown or global inputs, and compare predictions with instrumented full-suite executions to measure miss rate and savings.

setup.summary: A Python CI helper selects tests only by matching changed file paths to adjacent test directories.

acceptanceCriteria: Changes are computed from the correct merge base and include renames, deletions, and untracked CI inputs as configured.
Selection traces static, generated, observed runtime, configuration, and declared global dependencies.
Unknown resolution and graph gaps trigger a documented conservative fallback.
Each selected test has a machine-readable causal explanation and validation reports quantify misses.
hiddenChecks: Changing a code generator selects consumers of its outputs even when generated files are absent from the diff.
A renamed shared fixture selects both prior and current dependents.
Synthetic historical changes achieve zero false negatives against instrumented executions.
hazards: using HEAD parent instead of merge base

tasks.title: Reproducible Provenance-Signed Release
tasks.prompt: Implement a release pipeline that builds identical artifacts from the same source, generates an SBOM and verifiable provenance, signs by digest using short-lived identity, and promotes the exact tested bytes. Normalize archives, timestamps, paths, ordering, locale, and generated metadata; pin toolchains and dependencies; and make retries idempotent. Verification must work offline from the artifact, trust roots, and attached attestations.

setup.summary: A GitHub Actions repository rebuilds separately for publish and embeds host paths and current timestamps in archives.

acceptanceCriteria: Two clean builds of the same revision produce identical artifact digests.
SBOM and provenance bind source revision, builder identity, materials, invocation, and artifact digest.
Signing uses a pinned trust policy and promotion references the tested digest without rebuilding.
Tag or job retries cannot overwrite a different artifact for an existing immutable version.
hiddenChecks: Builds under different workspace paths, time zones, and locales remain byte-identical.
Offline verification rejects an artifact whose bytes differ from the attested digest.
A dependency or toolchain lock change appears in provenance materials and changes the artifact identity.

tasks.title: Semantics-Preserving API Codemod
tasks.prompt: Create a codemod migrating a deprecated callback API to promises across a large TypeScript monorepo. Handle aliases, namespace imports, re-exports, overloaded signatures, methods, callbacks with multiple success values, early returns, and mixed error conventions. Transform only type-resolved targets, preserve comments and formatting where practical, emit actionable TODOs for ambiguous cases, and make repeated runs produce no changes.

setup.summary: A jscodeshift script matches callee names textually and produces incorrect async control flow for nested callbacks.

acceptanceCriteria: Only calls resolving to the deprecated symbols are transformed.
Error, success, multiple-value, return, and this-binding semantics match the migration specification.
Unsupported ambiguous flows remain unchanged with a source-ranged TODO report.
Output type-checks, preserves meaningful trivia, and is idempotent after formatting.
hiddenChecks: A same-named local function is not transformed while a re-exported alias is.
Nested callback returns do not become unintended outer-function returns.
Running the codemod twice yields no diff and identical TODO reports.
hazards: blindly adding async to public APIs

tasks.title: Deterministic Lockfile Conflict Resolver
tasks.prompt: Implement a semantic merge driver for the supplied workspace lockfile format. Parse the base, ours, and theirs graphs; combine compatible manifest intent; resolve packages using an offline metadata snapshot and policy; preserve peer and platform variants; and emit canonical ordering and integrity values. When no policy-compliant solution exists, fail with a minimal dependency explanation rather than choosing one textual side.

setup.summary: A Rust merge tool chooses the larger text hunk, frequently creating parseable but semantically inconsistent lockfiles.

acceptanceCriteria: Merge derives intent from the three inputs and validates the result against workspace manifests.
Resolution honors versions, peer dependencies, platform variants, integrity, and repository policy.
Equivalent inputs emit byte-identical canonical lockfiles independent of hash iteration.
Unsatisfiable merges report a small causal constraint set and do not modify the target.
hiddenChecks: Commuting ours and theirs produces the same result when manifest intent is symmetric.
Peer variants with identical versions but different contexts remain distinct.
An offline metadata snapshot prevents network access and makes resolution repeatable.

tasks.title: Versioned Plugin ABI Compatibility
tasks.prompt: Design and implement a stable C ABI between the host and dynamically loaded plugins across two released interface versions. Add size-tagged structs, negotiated capability tables, explicit allocator ownership, error lifetimes, thread-safety declarations, and graceful rejection of incompatible plugins. The host must isolate plugin panics or exceptions at the boundary and support old plugins without recompilation while new optional functions remain discoverable.

setup.summary: A C++ host exposes STL types and virtual classes directly, causing crashes when compiler or runtime versions differ.

acceptanceCriteria: The public boundary uses C-compatible fixed-width types, size or version tags, and explicit calling conventions.
Host and plugin negotiate optional capabilities without reading beyond either side's structure size.
Allocation, string, handle, callback, error, and thread ownership rules are encoded and documented.
Version-one binary fixtures load in the version-two host and incompatible binaries fail diagnostically.
hiddenChecks: A truncated older function table never causes an out-of-bounds function read.
Cross-runtime allocation is released by the allocator that created it.
A plugin exception or Rust panic cannot unwind through the C boundary.

tasks.title: Cross-Platform CLI Process Launcher
tasks.prompt: Implement the process layer for a CLI that runs tools on Unix and Windows without invoking a shell by default. Preserve exact argument boundaries, Unicode, working directory, selected environment, signal forwarding, exit status, and streamed stdout and stderr. Support explicit shell mode with a visible warning, response files for command-length limits, process-tree cancellation, and secret-safe diagnostics.

setup.summary: A Go CLI joins arguments into one command string, corrupting quoting and enabling injection on several platforms.

acceptanceCriteria: Default execution passes an argument vector directly and preserves empty, Unicode, and metacharacter arguments.
Cancellation forwards the documented signals and terminates the complete owned process tree after grace.
Output streaming avoids deadlock, preserves per-stream bytes, and supports bounded capture.
Diagnostics redact configured secrets and distinguish spawn failure, signal, and numeric exit.
hiddenChecks: Adversarial shell metacharacters create no files and arrive as one literal child argument.
A child filling stdout and stderr concurrently cannot deadlock the parent.
Cancellation removes a spawned grandchild on both Unix and Windows fixtures.

tasks.title: Race-Free Incremental Watch Mode
tasks.prompt: Repair watch mode for a compiler that misses atomic-save events, rebuilds stale graphs, and publishes outputs from obsolete builds. Normalize platform-specific create, modify, rename, and delete bursts into content snapshots; debounce without losing events during a build; cancel or supersede obsolete work; and atomically publish only the newest complete generation. Recover from watcher overflow by reconciling the full tree.

setup.summary: A Node.js compiler clears a changed-file set before asynchronous builds and writes output directly as each file completes.

acceptanceCriteria: Event bursts reduce to an authoritative content snapshot including rename and deletion semantics.
Changes arriving during a build schedule a newer generation and cannot be cleared by the older one.
Only the latest successful generation atomically publishes a coherent output set.
Overflow, watcher restart, and platform differences trigger safe reconciliation.
hiddenChecks: Atomic-save rename patterns on macOS, Linux, and Windows fixtures all rebuild the target once logically.
A slower old build finishing last cannot overwrite newer output.
Watcher overflow followed by deletion removes stale generated output after full reconciliation.
hazards: assuming watcher events are complete history

tasks.title: Stateful HTTP/2 Frame Engine
tasks.prompt: Complete an HTTP/2 connection engine below the request layer. Parse frames incrementally, enforce connection and stream state transitions, assemble header blocks across CONTINUATION frames, apply HPACK table limits, maintain flow-control windows, prioritize control frames, and distinguish stream from connection errors. Input may split at any byte and peers may interleave legal frames while local writes are backpressured.

setup.summary: A Rust protocol crate handles complete frames but ignores continuation sequencing and connection-level flow-control edge cases.

acceptanceCriteria: Every frame type is length-checked and processed according to current connection and stream state.
Header blocks require contiguous valid continuation sequences and respect decoded-size limits.
Stream and connection windows use overflow-safe accounting and resume writers on WINDOW_UPDATE.
Protocol failures emit the correctly scoped error while preserving unaffected streams when allowed.
hiddenChecks: Every byte-level segmentation of a reference trace produces the same events.
Interleaving a non-CONTINUATION frame inside a header block yields the required connection error.
Window exhaustion stalls only data and cannot block PING, RST_STREAM, or GOAWAY.

tasks.title: WebSocket Fragmentation and Close State
tasks.prompt: Implement a compliant WebSocket peer supporting fragmented data messages, interleaved control frames, masking rules, per-message size limits, UTF-8 validation across fragments, ping and pong liveness, and the full closing handshake. The reader and writer operate concurrently over one connection; serialize frames without blocking pong behind a large message and ensure cancellation cannot leave a partial frame that another writer continues.

setup.summary: A Go library treats each frame as a message and closes the socket immediately on any local shutdown.

acceptanceCriteria: Fragmented text and binary messages assemble with legal control-frame interleaving.
Masking, control-frame, opcode, close-code, UTF-8, and size rules are enforced at the correct scope.
Control frames have bounded write latency under data backpressure.
Close performs one valid handshake with deadline and reports clean versus abnormal termination.
hiddenChecks: A multibyte UTF-8 scalar split across three fragments validates correctly.
Canceling a large write cannot corrupt the next frame on the wire.
Simultaneous local and remote close emits at most one close frame and terminates cleanly.

tasks.title: Caching Recursive DNS Resolver
tasks.prompt: Finish a recursive DNS resolver with iterative referrals, bailiwick-aware glue, CNAME and DNAME handling, positive and negative caching, request coalescing, UDP truncation fallback to TCP, and strict work limits. Cache TTLs using monotonic elapsed time, distinguish NXDOMAIN from NODATA using SOA data, prevent referral loops, and randomize query identity sufficiently for the provided threat model.

setup.summary: A Java resolver follows referrals recursively but caches all additional records and treats every empty answer as NXDOMAIN.

acceptanceCriteria: Iterative resolution validates message IDs, questions, sections, compression pointers, and referral progress.
Only in-bailiwick useful glue is cached and out-of-bailiwick names resolve independently.
Positive, NXDOMAIN, and NODATA cache entries apply correct bounded TTL semantics.
Concurrent identical lookups coalesce while each caller retains its own deadline.
hiddenChecks: A malicious compression-pointer loop and oversized name fail without recursion overflow.
Poison records in an unrelated additional section never enter cache.
A truncated UDP answer retries over TCP and preserves the original caller deadline.

tasks.title: QUIC Loss Recovery Simulator
tasks.prompt: Implement QUIC-style loss detection and congestion control in the supplied packet-level simulator. Maintain separate packet number spaces, RTT estimation with acknowledged delay rules, packet and time thresholds, probe timeout backoff, bytes in flight, NewReno recovery, and persistent-congestion detection. ACK frames may be reordered or duplicate ranges, and handshake key discard must retire timers and outstanding metadata safely.

setup.summary: A Rust simulator retransmits on a fixed timeout and applies one global packet sequence and RTT sample.

acceptanceCriteria: Sent and acknowledged state is isolated by packet number space and duplicate ACK ranges are harmless.
RTT, loss threshold, and probe timers follow the supplied transport specification.
Congestion window changes once per recovery epoch with correct bytes-in-flight accounting.
Discarding handshake keys removes obsolete packets and timers without counting false loss.
hiddenChecks: Reference traces for reordering, PTO, and persistent congestion match expected state transitions.
ACKing a packet twice never underflows bytes in flight or grows the congestion window twice.
Timer calculations remain monotonic and overflow-safe under extreme simulated durations.
hazards: one packet space for all encryption levels
retransmitting packet bytes instead of frame intent

tasks.title: Backpressured TCP Proxy With Half-Close
tasks.prompt: Repair a bidirectional TCP proxy so it preserves half-close semantics, applies bounded buffers in both directions, propagates cancellation and deadlines, and does not leak connections when one side stalls. EOF from one read side must flush pending bytes then close only the opposite write half while the reverse direction may continue. Collect accurate byte and termination metrics without treating expected shutdown errors as failures.

setup.summary: A C# proxy launches two unbounded copy tasks and closes both sockets when either direction reaches EOF.

acceptanceCriteria: Each direction has bounded buffering and applies transport backpressure to a slow peer.
EOF drains queued bytes and performs the correct write-half shutdown without killing reverse traffic.
Fatal error, deadline, or cancellation terminates both pumps and disposes every owned resource.
Metrics distinguish clean EOF, timeout, cancellation, reset, and proxy fault.
hiddenChecks: A request-side half-close still permits a multi-megabyte response to finish.
A nonreading destination cannot grow process memory beyond the configured buffer bounds.
Simultaneous reset and cancellation complete once without unobserved task exceptions.
hazards: closing both sides on first EOF
waiting forever for the sibling pump

tasks.title: Streaming Multipart Parser
tasks.prompt: Implement a streaming multipart/form-data parser for uploads whose boundaries and headers can split across arbitrary chunks. Correctly distinguish partial boundary prefixes from payload, parse quoted parameters, reject ambiguous line endings and duplicate security-sensitive headers, and stream each part under per-part and aggregate limits. The algorithm must use bounded look-behind and remain linear on inputs containing long near-boundary repetitions.

setup.summary: A Node.js server buffers the entire body and searches with repeated indexOf calls that become quadratic.

acceptanceCriteria: Parsing is invariant to every legal chunk boundary, including boundaries split byte by byte.
Boundary recognition, terminal delimiters, line endings, and header syntax follow the documented grammar.
Part bytes stream to a sink with bounded look-behind, header, count, part, and total limits.
Near-match adversarial payload remains linear and failure cleans up all partial sinks.
hiddenChecks: Payload ending in every proper boundary prefix is preserved until the next chunk disambiguates it.
Quoted filenames containing separators and escaped quotes parse without path interpretation.
Millions of near-boundary prefixes complete within the time and memory budget.

tasks.title: Gap-Free Resumable SSE Feed
tasks.prompt: Implement a resumable Server-Sent Events endpoint backed by a durable ordered event log. Parse and honor Last-Event-ID, bridge the race between historical catch-up and live subscription, send heartbeat comments, bound slow-client buffers, and close with retry guidance when retention has removed the requested position. Encode multiline data and optional event names correctly, and stop all work promptly on disconnect.

setup.summary: A Kotlin endpoint reads history then subscribes live, losing events committed between those operations.

acceptanceCriteria: Catch-up and live handoff use a position protocol that cannot create a gap or duplicate emission.
Last-Event-ID validation distinguishes current, unknown, malformed, and retention-expired positions.
Wire formatting handles multiline data, event, id, retry, and heartbeat comment fields.
Slow clients have a bounded policy and disconnect cancels database and subscription work.
hiddenChecks: An event committed at every handoff interleaving is delivered exactly once.
A paused client cannot grow the hub queue beyond its configured bound.
Reconnect after the last delivered ID resumes with the next event and no blank synthetic event.

tasks.title: Idempotency-Aware gRPC Retry Layer
tasks.prompt: Implement client-side retries and optional hedging for unary gRPC calls. Policies are method-specific and may retry only declared idempotent operations and eligible status codes within the original deadline and retry budget. Respect server pushback, exponential jittered backoff, per-attempt metadata, and cancellation; commit to the first response that reaches the protocol commitment point and cancel losing hedges without corrupting metrics.

setup.summary: A Go interceptor retries all UNAVAILABLE responses with a fresh timeout and can duplicate non-idempotent mutations.

acceptanceCriteria: Only configured idempotent methods and retryable pre-commit outcomes receive additional attempts.
Every attempt is bounded by the original caller deadline and a shared retry-token budget.
Backoff uses deterministic-testable jitter and honors valid server retry pushback.
Hedges commit one winner, cancel losers, and record logical-call and attempt metrics separately.
hiddenChecks: A non-idempotent method receives exactly one transport attempt on every status.
Headers that establish commitment suppress retry of a later stream failure.
Caller cancellation during backoff or a hedge terminates every attempt immediately.
hazards: counting hedges as separate user calls

tasks.title: Extensible Binary Protocol Negotiation
tasks.prompt: Design and implement version negotiation plus codecs for a long-lived binary agent protocol. Peers advertise version ranges, mandatory features, optional extensions, compression, and frame limits. Select a deterministic compatible profile, preserve unknown length-delimited fields for proxying, reject unknown mandatory features, and prevent downgrade below local policy. Old and new peers must interoperate without interpreting the same bytes differently.

setup.summary: A Rust client and server compare one integer version and reuse field tags with changed meanings across releases.

acceptanceCriteria: Negotiation chooses a deterministic highest policy-allowed intersection or reports the exact incompatibility.
Mandatory and optional features have distinct handling and no field tag changes meaning within a version.
Decoders bound lengths, depth, decompression, and integer arithmetic before allocation.
Unknown extension data round-trips through intermediaries when its envelope is valid.
hiddenChecks: Every pair in the old and new fixture matrix either interoperates or rejects predictably.
A peer advertising a high version but missing a mandatory feature cannot force downgrade ambiguity.
Fuzzed unknown fields preserve byte payloads without being interpreted.

tasks.title: Checksum-Verified Resumable Upload
tasks.prompt: Implement a resumable upload protocol for large artifacts over unreliable HTTP. Create an upload session with fixed total size and digest, accept idempotent content-range chunks in arbitrary retry order, reject overlaps with different bytes, expose durable progress, and atomically publish only after full coverage and streaming checksum verification. Concurrent requests for the same range must not corrupt temporary storage.

setup.summary: A Python server appends chunks to one file and trusts a client-reported final offset.

acceptanceCriteria: Session identity binds expected size, digest, media metadata, and authorization principal.
Range parsing and coverage use exact inclusive or exclusive semantics with overflow-safe bounds.
Identical retries are idempotent while conflicting overlaps reject without modifying accepted bytes.
Completion verifies full coverage and digest before atomic artifact publication.
hiddenChecks: Concurrent duplicate and adjacent ranges produce one correct artifact.
A one-byte overlap with different data is rejected and prior accepted coverage remains intact.
Restart between final write and publication resumes to either verified temporary or complete artifact.

tasks.title: Deterministic Production Race Replayer
tasks.prompt: Diagnose an intermittent lost-update bug in a collaborative service using the supplied redacted production event trace. Build a deterministic replay harness that controls task scheduling, clocks, random values, and injected I/O completions; minimize the failing schedule; identify the violated invariant; and implement the smallest safe fix. The regression must fail on the original implementation without probabilistic sleeps and pass across many generated schedules.

setup.summary: A Kotlin coroutine service occasionally acknowledges two edits while persisting only one, but existing stress tests are flaky.

acceptanceCriteria: The replay captures all nondeterministic inputs needed to reproduce the failure exactly.
A minimized schedule demonstrates the invariant violation on the unfixed code.
The fix addresses the causal race without globally serializing unrelated documents.
Regression and generated schedule tests are sleep-free and deterministic.
hiddenChecks: Perturbing irrelevant event timing does not make the harness nondeterministic.
The original bug reproduces from a compact checked-in schedule in every run.
Throughput for independent document IDs remains concurrent after the fix.

tasks.title: Correct Circuit Breaker State Machine
tasks.prompt: Implement a concurrency-safe circuit breaker with rolling failure statistics, minimum volume, open duration, half-open probe limits, outcome classification, and monotonic time. Calls already admitted when the breaker opens may finish, but their results must update the correct generation. Configuration can reload at runtime without resetting useful history incorrectly. Expose state transitions and rejected calls as low-cardinality metrics.

setup.summary: A C# client library uses lifetime counters and permits every caller through simultaneously when open duration expires.

acceptanceCriteria: Rolling buckets and outcome classification implement the documented volume and rate thresholds.
Exactly the configured number of probes enter half-open per generation.
State deadlines use monotonic time and generation checks prevent stale completions from corrupting new state.
Live policy changes preserve or reset history according to explicit compatibility rules.
hiddenChecks: One hundred callers at the open deadline admit only the configured probe count.
A slow success from before opening cannot close a later breaker generation.
Clock rollback in the fake wall clock does not extend or shorten open duration.

tasks.title: Lossless Graceful Service Shutdown
tasks.prompt: Implement graceful shutdown for an API that serves HTTP, consumes jobs, runs scheduled maintenance, and batches telemetry. On termination, fail readiness, stop admitting new work, drain keep-alive requests, stop claiming jobs, extend or return owned leases, flush durable outcomes, and finally close dependencies in order under one overall deadline. A second signal must force termination, and every phase must be idempotent.

setup.summary: A Go service cancels one root context immediately, interrupting committed responses and abandoning claimed jobs.

acceptanceCriteria: Readiness changes before listeners stop admitting new externally routed requests.
In-flight requests and jobs receive bounded drain behavior consistent with their commit points.
Resources close in dependency order within a shared deadline and cleanup tolerates repeated calls.
A second termination signal bypasses remaining grace without deadlocking.
hiddenChecks: Termination during response commit neither reports success with lost state nor duplicates a retryable effect.
A job lease is renewed or safely returned until its outcome is durable.
A stuck telemetry sink cannot consume more than its allocated shutdown budget.
hazards: canceling all work before admission stops

tasks.title: Atomic Live Configuration Reload
tasks.prompt: Implement live reload of layered configuration from file, environment, and a remote source. Parse into an immutable candidate, validate cross-field invariants, resolve secrets without logging them, and atomically publish one version so readers never observe mixed old and new fields. Components that require preparation must stage resources before commit and roll them back on failure; nonreloadable changes must be rejected with exact diagnostics.

setup.summary: A Rust daemon mutates a shared configuration struct field by field and partially applies invalid reloads.

acceptanceCriteria: Layer precedence and provenance are deterministic for every effective field.
Readers obtain one immutable configuration version and cannot observe partial updates.
Reloadable resource changes prepare, commit, and retire old resources with rollback on preparation failure.
Diagnostics identify invalid and nonreloadable fields while redacting secret values.
hiddenChecks: Concurrent readers see only the complete old or complete new invariant-related field tuple.
Failure opening a replacement TLS certificate leaves the previous listener and configuration active.
Rapid file event bursts converge to the newest valid content rather than an intermediate version.
hazards: including secret values in validation errors

tasks.title: Crash-Recoverable Durable Work Queue
tasks.prompt: Finish a disk-backed work queue with enqueue, claim, acknowledge, retry delay, and dead-letter operations. Define durability at each API return, use a checksummed append log plus recoverable index, truncate torn tails, compact online without losing concurrent writes, and make redelivery safe after worker crash. Disk-full and fsync failures must surface without acknowledging operations that recovery cannot reproduce.

setup.summary: A C++ queue updates an mmap index before appending records and corrupts state when killed during compaction.

acceptanceCriteria: The implementation documents and meets a precise durability point for every successful mutation.
Recovery validates records, ignores or truncates torn tails, and reconstructs a consistent index.
Online compaction captures concurrent appends and atomically installs a complete new generation.
Claim expiry and acknowledgment transitions produce at-least-once delivery without losing accepted work.
hiddenChecks: Power-loss injection after every write and sync recovers exactly the acknowledged operation prefix.
Disk-full during enqueue or compaction leaves the prior durable queue usable.
A worker crash after claim redelivers the item and a stale acknowledgment cannot remove a new claim.

tasks.title: Time-Zone-Correct Recurring Scheduler
tasks.prompt: Implement a persistent recurring scheduler for user-defined local-time rules across daylight-saving gaps, folds, time-zone database updates, clock jumps, restarts, and multiple scheduler replicas. Make gap and ambiguity policy explicit per schedule, claim occurrences idempotently, never derive the next run only from the last wall-clock instant, and expose both intended local time and resolved UTC instant for audit.

setup.summary: A Java service adds 24 hours to the prior UTC timestamp and runs duplicate jobs when two replicas poll.

acceptanceCriteria: Rules persist local recurrence, zone identifier, gap policy, fold policy, and time-zone data version.
Occurrence generation is based on logical local sequence and records resolved instants explicitly.
Replica claims use a durable unique occurrence identity and lease or transaction semantics.
Clock jumps, downtime catch-up, and time-zone rule updates follow documented bounded policies.
hiddenChecks: Spring gaps and autumn folds in multiple zones produce exactly the configured occurrences.
Two replicas polling the same due occurrence execute its logical effect once.
Restart after a long outage catches up only the allowed window without drifting future local times.

tasks.title: Causally Complete Distributed Tracing
tasks.prompt: Repair tracing across HTTP, a message broker, background fan-out, retries, and batch processing. Propagate standards-compliant context without trusting arbitrary baggage, represent producers and consumers with correct span links, keep retries and logical operations distinguishable, and ensure tail sampling retains complete error traces. Bound attribute cardinality, redact sensitive values, and add trace-based assertions rather than checking only emitted span counts.

setup.summary: A Python system starts unrelated spans in consumers and copies all incoming headers into span attributes.

acceptanceCriteria: HTTP and messaging context follows the relevant propagation and semantic conventions.
Fan-out, batch, and retry relationships use parentage or links that preserve causal truth.
Sampling configuration retains required error traces without orphaning partial graphs.
Attributes and baggage are allowlisted, bounded, and redacted before export.
hiddenChecks: A batch consuming messages from three traces links all causes without inventing one common parent.
Retry attempts share a logical operation identity but have distinct attempt spans and metrics.
Injected high-cardinality and secret baggage neither reaches export nor explodes series counts.
hazards: forcing every message into one parent chain

tasks.title: Poison-Message Quarantine Workflow
tasks.prompt: Implement handling for messages that repeatedly fail processing. Classify transient versus permanent outcomes, apply bounded jittered retry without head-of-line blocking, atomically move terminal failures to a quarantine stream with original envelope and diagnostic provenance, and provide safe replay after code or data repair. Replay must preserve identity, prevent loops, and be auditable without retaining secrets in clear text.

setup.summary: A Node.js consumer retries every exception immediately and one malformed event stalls its entire ordered partition.

acceptanceCriteria: Retry decisions distinguish declared transient, permanent, schema, and unknown failures.
Backoff is bounded and partition strategy prevents one poison item from busy-looping or silently reordering protected keys.
Quarantine publication and source position advancement cannot lose the failed message.
Replay requires authorization and reason, retains original identity, and records lineage and outcome.
hiddenChecks: A malformed message reaches quarantine once while later independent keys continue.
Crash between quarantine send and source commit does not create two replayable logical records.
Replaying an unrepaired item cannot bounce indefinitely between primary and quarantine topics.
hazards: assigning a new identity on replay

tasks.title: Adaptive Brownout and Load Shedding
tasks.prompt: Add overload protection to an API whose dependencies collapse during demand spikes. Use concurrency and queue delay signals to reject early, reserve capacity for health and high-priority traffic, and progressively disable optional expensive features through a hysteretic brownout controller. Preserve correctness of core responses, publish honest degradation metadata, and prove recovery does not oscillate when load hovers near thresholds.

setup.summary: A Java API accepts unbounded work and retries downstream timeouts, amplifying traffic until every endpoint fails.

acceptanceCriteria: Admission uses bounded concurrency and queue-delay or saturation signals before downstream work begins.
Priority classes have explicit reservations and cannot borrow in a way that starves protected traffic.
Brownout levels disable only declared optional work and transition with hysteresis and minimum dwell.
Responses and metrics distinguish rejection, degraded success, and full success.
hiddenChecks: A sharp burst preserves the high-priority latency objective while rejecting bounded low-priority load.
Near-threshold oscillating demand does not flap brownout levels on every sample.
Downstream retry amplification remains within the declared retry budget during overload.

tasks.title: Deterministic Cross-Layer Fault Harness
tasks.prompt: Build a deterministic fault-injection framework spanning filesystem, database client, network transport, clock, and process lifecycle boundaries. Tests must target named semantic fault points, compose faults with seeded schedules, record a replayable trace, and assert post-recovery invariants. Production builds must impose near-zero overhead and cannot activate injection through untrusted request input.

setup.summary: A Go service has scattered random failure flags and nondeterministic chaos tests that cannot reproduce CI failures.

acceptanceCriteria: Fault points have stable semantic names and typed actions rather than source-line coupling.
A seed and recorded nondeterministic inputs reproduce the same ordered injection trace.
Scenarios compose delay, error, partial success, crash, and clock actions under explicit budgets.
Injection is compile-time or authenticated-test isolated from production requests.
hiddenChecks: A failing generated scenario shrinks to a smaller replayable fault schedule.
Renaming or refactoring unrelated functions does not change semantic fault selection.
A production configuration cannot enable faults through headers, environment inherited from a child, or public RPC.

tasks.title: Dirty-Tree-Aware Patch Planner
tasks.prompt: Implement a patch planner for an autonomous coding agent operating in a dirty Git worktree. Classify baseline, staged, unstaged, untracked, and agent-produced content; calculate edits against the live file; refuse ambiguous overlapping hunks; and preserve user changes byte-for-byte outside authorized regions. Produce a preview that attributes every line change and a rollback patch containing only the agent's confirmed modifications.

setup.summary: A Rust agent snapshots HEAD and writes generated files wholesale, overwriting user edits made before and during a task.

acceptanceCriteria: The planner records HEAD, index, live baseline, and agent intent without conflating ownership.
Nonoverlapping edits merge against current content and ambiguous overlaps stop with precise context.
Preview labels additions, removals, and conflicts by provenance without staging automatically.
Rollback reverses only still-matching agent-owned changes and never restores unrelated content from HEAD.
hiddenChecks: Preexisting staged and unstaged hunks remain byte-identical after apply and rollback.
A user edit arriving between preview and apply triggers revalidation rather than overwrite.
Line-ending and missing-final-newline differences do not expand the authorized patch.

tasks.title: Shell-Aware Command Policy Engine
tasks.prompt: Build a command authorization engine for agent-proposed shell operations. Parse rather than substring-match pipelines, logical lists, redirections, substitutions, environment assignments, globs, and nested shells; resolve executable identity and workspace-relative paths; split approval decisions at control operators; and explain the exact risky capability. Default execution should use argv without a shell, with a separately approved path for shell syntax.

setup.summary: A Go agent allows commands when their string starts with an approved prefix, enabling injection through control operators and substitutions.

acceptanceCriteria: Policy decisions operate on parsed commands, arguments, redirections, substitutions, and control-flow segments.
Executable and path capabilities are resolved without trusting aliases, PATH shadowing, or unresolved broad targets.
Approval descriptions identify each material read, write, network, privilege, and destructive capability.
Non-shell execution preserves literal arguments and shell mode requires explicit scoped authorization.
hiddenChecks: Approved benign prefixes cannot authorize appended pipes, substitutions, redirections, or nested shell payloads.
A workspace executable shadowing a system command is identified by its resolved target.
Fuzzed parse failures default to refusal without executing any prefix.

tasks.title: Secret-Safe Repository Context Index
tasks.prompt: Implement the repository indexing pipeline used to select context for an LLM. Respect ignore rules and explicit sensitive zones, detect secrets before chunks reach embeddings or logs, retain source ranges for later citation, and update incrementally across renames and edits. Treat file contents and filenames as untrusted data that cannot change agent policy. Deletion must remove derived chunks and cache entries by content lineage.

setup.summary: A Python indexer uploads every text-like file, logs rejected content, and leaves embeddings after source deletion.

acceptanceCriteria: Discovery follows repository ignore, size, binary, symlink, and configured sensitive-path policy.
Secret scanning and content declassification happen before embedding, caching, telemetry, or error serialization.
Chunks retain immutable content digest, canonical source identity, byte range, language, and derivation version.
Rename, modification, deletion, and policy change update every derived artifact without stale lineage.
hiddenChecks: Canary credentials in source, filename, parse error, and binary-adjacent text never reach the fake embedder or logs.
A deleted file removes all chunk, embedding, and retrieval entries that derive from it.
Prompt-like instructions inside comments remain quoted repository data and cannot modify indexing policy.

tasks.title: Symlink-Safe Workspace Edit Transaction
tasks.prompt: Harden file editing so an agent can modify only regular files beneath approved workspace roots despite symlinks, hard links, path swaps, case folding, and concurrent directory renames. Resolve and open paths descriptor-relatively, validate identity before replacement, write a sibling temporary with safe permissions, fsync as required, and atomically rename. Reject special files and never follow a newly introduced link between validation and write.

setup.summary: A C++ editing service validates realpath once and later opens the original string path for truncating writes.

acceptanceCriteria: Every path component and final target is resolved under an approved root without following disallowed links.
Identity and type checks remain valid through atomic replacement despite concurrent path mutations.
Temporary data, file metadata policy, data sync, rename, and directory sync follow the durability contract.
Case, separator, normalization, special-file, hard-link, and platform behavior are documented and tested.
hiddenChecks: A directory swapped for a symlink after validation cannot redirect the write outside the workspace.
Editing a FIFO or device path fails without blocking or triggering device behavior.
A hard-linked sensitive target is rejected under the configured single-link policy.

tasks.title: Recoverable Multi-File Refactoring
tasks.prompt: Implement a transactional refactoring layer for agent edits spanning source, tests, generated metadata, renames, and deletions. Preflight expected file identities, stage a complete candidate tree, run format and validation against that candidate, then publish with a durable journal. A process crash during publication must recover to the complete before or after state, and rollback must not erase user edits made after publication.

setup.summary: A Java refactoring tool overwrites files sequentially and leaves mixed API versions when formatting or validation fails.

acceptanceCriteria: Preflight records content and identity expectations for every create, edit, rename, and delete.
Formatting and validation run against the fully staged candidate rather than a partially modified workspace.
The durable journal and recovery protocol converge to one complete state after any publication crash point.
Rollback uses compare-before-revert and stops on post-publication user changes.
hiddenChecks: Crash injection after every journal and rename operation recovers no mixed refactoring state.
A user edit after successful publication is preserved when rollback is requested.
Rename cycles and case-only renames work on both case-sensitive and case-insensitive fixtures.

tasks.title: Prompt-Injection-Resistant Tool Output
tasks.prompt: Build the boundary that ingests compiler output, test logs, web responses, and repository files into an agent loop. Preserve the data needed for diagnosis while marking source, trust, and truncation; prevent untrusted text from being interpreted as policy, approval, tool results, or completion evidence; and require structured trusted channels for actions. Add adversarial fixtures that imitate system messages, approval tokens, ANSI controls, and JSON tool envelopes.

setup.summary: A TypeScript agent concatenates raw tool stdout into its control prompt and detects success from magic text in the stream.

acceptanceCriteria: Every content block carries immutable provenance, trust class, byte count, and truncation metadata.
Only schema-validated tool control channels can request actions, approvals, or terminal status.
Untrusted text is quoted and delimited consistently without relying on a secret sentinel.
ANSI, control characters, oversized lines, nested encodings, and fake envelopes are sanitized under bounded work.
hiddenChecks: A failing test named with a fake approval and success transcript cannot change agent control state.
Tool stdout containing a valid-looking JSON action remains content rather than executable control.
Truncation cannot remove provenance delimiters or make an untrusted suffix appear trusted.
hazards: trusting JSON based only on syntax

tasks.title: Safe Parallel Git Worktree Integration
tasks.prompt: Implement integration of changes produced by parallel coding-agent worktrees. Record each task's base commit and owned patch, detect overlapping semantic and textual edits, order dependent patches, and apply through a temporary integration index without disturbing the user's current index or worktree. Conflicts must remain explicit with provenance from each agent; abort and retry operations must be idempotent and recoverable.

setup.summary: A Rust orchestrator runs git cherry-pick in the user's worktree and occasionally stages unrelated local files.

acceptanceCriteria: Integration uses recorded bases and an isolated temporary index or worktree.
Patch dependency and overlap analysis determines safe order without silently choosing winners.
Conflict artifacts identify base, current, each agent source, and affected task ownership.
Success, abort, crash recovery, and retry leave the user's original index and unrelated files unchanged.
hiddenChecks: Preexisting staged changes remain byte-for-byte and mode-for-mode identical after integration.
Two agents editing different functions on nearby lines merge, while same-symbol conflicts remain explicit.
Crash during conflict materialization can be retried without duplicate commits or stale lock files.
hazards: integrating in the user's active index
assuming patches share the same base

tasks.title: Capability-Scoped Approval Workflow
tasks.prompt: Implement an approval system for agent actions with explicit capabilities, exact targets, risk summaries, expiration, and single-use or reusable scope. Bind approval to a canonical action digest so changed commands, paths, network destinations, or payloads require new consent. Prevent confused-deputy reuse across tasks and users, persist an audit trail, and make denial or timeout leave no partially executed side effect.

setup.summary: A Go agent stores a boolean approved flag per conversation and reuses it for later materially different commands.

acceptanceCriteria: Requests describe actor, task, capability, canonical targets, material parameters, risk, and duration.
Consent is cryptographically or transactionally bound to the exact canonical action digest and scope.
Execution atomically consumes single-use approvals or verifies valid reusable constraints before effects.
Every request, decision, use, denial, expiry, and mismatch produces a tamper-evident audit event.
hiddenChecks: Changing only a redirect target, output path, or hidden shell segment invalidates prior approval.
Approval from another task or user cannot authorize an otherwise identical action.
Two concurrent uses of a single-use approval allow exactly one execution.
hazards: consuming approval after the side effect

tasks.title: Evidence-Backed Completion Verifier
tasks.prompt: Build a verifier that prevents a coding agent from declaring completion without fresh, relevant evidence. Map requested outcomes to source changes, tests, builds, runtime checks, and external-state observations; record command, revision, environment, timestamp, exit, and bounded artifact digests; invalidate evidence after relevant edits; and distinguish passed, skipped, unavailable, and inferred claims. Untrusted tool text cannot self-certify success.

setup.summary: A Python agent marks tasks complete when stdout contains words like passed, even if tests ran before the final edit.

acceptanceCriteria: Completion claims decompose into explicit evidence requirements with relevance rules.
Evidence binds repository revision or content inputs, environment, invocation, outcome, and trusted producer.
Relevant subsequent edits invalidate stale evidence while unrelated edits retain it with an explanation.
Reports state verified, failed, unavailable, skipped, and inferred outcomes without collapsing them.
hiddenChecks: A passing test run before a changed covered source file cannot verify the final revision.
Fake passing text printed by a failing test process does not count as success.
A source-only check cannot substantiate a claim that a deployed GUI flow works.
hazards: equating source inspection with end-to-end verification

tasks.title: Bounded Autonomous Task Controller
tasks.prompt: Implement the top-level Krater Pro task controller that turns a user request into explicit goals, authorized scope, budgets, reversible actions, verification, and a truthful terminal state. It must make progress through recoverable failures, detect repeated blockers, avoid broadening permissions or editing unrelated files, stop runaway repair loops, and incorporate user interruptions as replace, amend, or question events without losing already confirmed work.

setup.summary: A TypeScript controller repeatedly replans from chat history, forgets action ownership, and reports success when its token budget ends.

acceptanceCriteria: Persistent state separates requested outcomes, assumptions, authorization, plan, actions, evidence, and blockers.
Every action is checked against target scope, capability approval, remaining budget, and reversibility policy.
Completion requires satisfied outcome evidence; exhaustion, cancellation, and repeated blockers have distinct truthful states.
Interruptions deterministically replace, amend, or query the active task while preserving attributable completed work.
hiddenChecks: Repeated failing fixes hit a bounded retry or novelty rule and cannot consume unlimited actions.
A budget reaching zero never changes an unmet task to complete.
A user question during execution receives an answer and then resumes without duplicating the last mutation.
